title: A finite type quasi-coherent module on an affine scheme is generated by finitely many global sections
statement: Let $U$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Then there are finitely many global sections $h_1,\dots,h_k\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)$ which generate $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], i.e. the map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus k}\to\mathcal G$, $(f_1,\dots,f_k)\mapsto\sum_jf_jh_j$, is surjective as a map of sheaves. In fact any finite family of elements generating the $\mathcal O_U(U)$-module $\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)$ (which is finitely generated) does.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PB (label lemma-finite-type-module) together with Schemes, Lemma 01IA (label schemes-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine: a quasi-coherent module on Spec R is the sheaf associated to its global sections); EGA I (1.3.13), cited in EGA II proof of 4.5.5

proof.text: Reduction and finiteness. Since $U$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], choose an isomorphism of schemes $g:U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}A$; transporting $\mathcal G$ along $g$ preserves quasi-coherence, finite type, global sections (with $g^\sharp:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_U(U)$) and the property that given sections generate [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] (surjectivity of a map of sheaves is invariant under homeomorphism with compatible sheaf isomorphisms). So we may assume $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Put $M=\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)$, an $R$-module. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a) to the scheme $X=U$ and its affine open $U$ itself: since $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], $M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. Hence a finite generating family $h_1,\dots,h_k$ of $M$ exists, and the first assertion follows from the second, which we now prove for an arbitrary such family. Let $\varphi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus k}\to\mathcal G$, $(f_j)\mapsto\sum_jf_jh_j$, be the map of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]; we must show $\varphi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module): finite type O_X-module M~ on Spec R iff M finite

proof.text: $\mathcal G\cong\widetilde M$ compatibly with sections. Let $\widetilde M$ with $\tau_U:M\to\Gamma(U,\widetilde M)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), since $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde M\to\mathcal G$ (the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_M$ under the adjunction (1), so $\varepsilon_U\circ\tau_U=\mathrm{id}_M$) is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Hence for every $x\in U$ the stalk map $\varepsilon_x:\widetilde M_x\to\mathcal G_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U,x}$-modules carrying the germ $\tau_U(m)_x$ to the germ $m_x$ of the global section $m\in M=\mathcal G(U)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine): a quasi-coherent module on Spec R is the sheaf associated to Gamma(X, F); Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions) for the mapping property

proof.text: Surjectivity on stalks. Let $x\in U$ correspond to the prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$; the germ map $\rho:R\to\mathcal O_{U,x}$ is a localization at $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1), so each $\rho(s)$, $s\in S$, is a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], $m\mapsto\tau_U(m)_x$ is a localization of $M$ at $S$, so every element of $\widetilde M_x$ has the form $\rho(s)^{-1}\tau_U(m)_x$; by step 2 every element of $\mathcal G_x$ has the form $\rho(s)^{-1}m_x$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S$. Write $m=\sum_jr_jh_j$ with $r_j\in R$ (the $h_j$ generate $M$). The stalk of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus k}$ at $x$ is $\mathcal O_{U,x}^{\oplus k}$ and $\varphi_x(g_1,\dots,g_k)=\sum_jg_j(h_j)_x$; since taking germs is compatible with the module structures, $\rho(s)^{-1}m_x=\sum_j\rho(s)^{-1}\rho(r_j)(h_j)_x=\varphi_x\big((\rho(s)^{-1}\rho(r_j))_j\big)$. So $\varphi_x$ is surjective for every $x\in U$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) (6),(7): stalks of O_X and of M~ are localizations

proof.text: Conclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks] (applied to the underlying presheaves of sets of $\varphi$), a map of sheaves on $U$ that is surjective on all stalks is surjective in the sense of sheaves. Hence $\varphi$ is surjective, i.e. $h_1,\dots,h_k$ generate $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections].

source.place: Sheaves, Definition 007U (5) and Lemma 0H7H (2): surjective maps of sheaves are those surjective on all stalks
